questions.question: What does the model actually receive when you send a list of chat messages?
options: One string with special tokens, rendered by the model's chat template
questions.explanation: The server renders messages into the exact text format the model was trained on.

questions.question: In llama3.2's template, what role header do tool results get?
questions.explanation: Llama 3 was trained with tool output under the ipython role.

questions.question: Where does llama3.2's template put tool definitions?
options: In the system message on every turn
Only inside the final user message
questions.explanation: So after a tool result, the last message isn't a user message, and the model sees no tools.

questions.question: How did the lesson verify the hand-rendered template?
options: By sending it in raw mode and comparing token counts and outputs with /api/chat
questions.explanation: Same tokens in and same output at temperature 0 is strong evidence of an exact match.

questions.question: The tool case was 6 tokens off even though the template was copied exactly. What does that show?
options: Servers can transform input (e.g. how tool definitions are serialised) outside the template
questions.explanation: The template only said {{ . }}; the formatting of tools happened in the server's code.

questions.question: What does prefill mean?
options: Writing the start of the assistant's reply yourself so the model continues from it
questions.explanation: Ending the prompt with '{"city": "' made the model reply 'Tokyo"}'.
